about: On-site self-check quizzes ('Now question it'). answer is the 0-based index of the right option. Passing = all correct (retries allowed).

prompts.q: Claude's first draft is close but too long. What's the best next move?
options: Start a new chat with a longer prompt
Reply with what to change: "Shorter, under 100 words"
Ask it to try again with no other guidance
prompts.why: Iterating in the same chat keeps everything Claude already understood. Say exactly what to change.

prompts.q: Which brief will most likely get a useful result on the first try?
options: "Write a 1-minute toast for my sister's 40th. She loves hiking and bad puns. Warm, not sappy."
"Write a toast like a professional writer would."
prompts.why: It says what, who, why and what good looks like. Hype words and role-play add little.

prompts.q: A quick test for whether your prompt is clear enough:
options: A smart friend with no background would understand it
prompts.why: If a friend with no context would be confused, Claude will be too.

models.q: For a quick rewrite of a two-line text message, which is usually the sensible choice?
options: The biggest model at maximum effort
Running it on every model to compare
It makes no difference to usage
models.why: Bigger and slower isn't better for small jobs, and higher effort uses more of your plan.

models.q: What does raising the effort level generally trade?
options: More time and usage for potentially better answers on hard problems
models.why: Effort is a dial between speed/usage and depth. Save high effort for jobs that need it.

models.q: You can't find a model you read about. The most likely reason?
options: Model availability depends on your plan and changes over time
models.why: Plans differ in which models they include, and names change. Check the Help Center.

discernment.q: Claude gives you a confident, well-written answer with a specific date. What should you do if the date matters?
options: Check it against a source you open yourself
Ask Claude if it's sure, and accept a yes
Rephrase the question until you like the answer
discernment.why: Confidence isn't evidence. Open a real source for anything that matters.

options: Agreeing with you just to please you
discernment.why: Models can drift toward agreeing with you. Ask it to argue the other side.

discernment.q: The strongest way to get an honest critique of something important Claude helped you make:
options: Ask the same chat "is this good?"
Paste it into a fresh chat and ask for the top problems
Skip review if it reads well
discernment.why: A fresh session has no attachment to the draft and catches different problems.

artifacts.q: What is an artifact in Claude?
options: Something Claude makes that you'd put in front of someone, opened beside the chat
artifacts.why: Docs, decks, designs, dashboards and small tools open as artifacts beside the chat.

artifacts.q: Before asking for an artifact, the most useful thing to specify is:
options: The format, audience, length and must-haves
artifacts.why: Specifying the output is the signature move of this arc.

artifacts.q: Who can see an artifact you've just made?
options: Only you, until you choose to share it
artifacts.why: Artifacts stay private until you share them, so read before you share.

designs.q: Which gets less generic design results?
options: Showing two or three examples you like

designs.q: Why ask for several design options?
options: Choosing between options is easier and better than correcting one

designs.q: A simple design system mostly helps by:
options: Keeping colors, fonts and spacing consistent across pieces
designs.why: Name your choices once and every piece can match.

data.q: A chart Claude placed in a document last week is:
options: A live feed that updates itself
A snapshot of the data at that time
data.why: Snapshots need a refresh when you want the latest.

data.q: The habit that matters most at the Data Bench:
options: Using as many colors as possible
Tracing every number back to a real source and spot-checking a few
data.why: Charts look trustworthy even when a number is wrong.

data.q: Claude's chart says 5 votes for mushrooms; your list shows 4. What now?
options: Tell Claude what you found and ask it to recount, then check again
data.why: Point to the discrepancy, have it fixed, and re-check.

motion.q: What should come before building an animation?
options: A short storyboard of the beats

motion.q: A good rule for on-screen text in a short explainer:
options: Keep it to a few words per screen
motion.why: People watch more than they read.

motion.q: Motion and video features in Claude:
options: Are identical on every plan forever
Vary by plan and change often, so check the Help Center
motion.why: Check what your account can do today.

projects.q: What does a Claude project give you that a single chat doesn't?
options: A workspace whose files and instructions apply to every chat in it
projects.why: A project is a workbench that remembers.

projects.q: Adding every file you have to a project usually:
options: Can distract Claude; the right context beats more context
projects.why: Feed it what it needs, not everything.

projects.q: Where should a rule like "always write plans as a table" go?
projects.why: Project instructions apply every time, so you don't repeat yourself.

options: A permission for Claude to read from or act in one of your apps
A browser extension that blocks ads
connectors.why: Connectors plug Claude into apps you already use.

connectors.q: Most connectors use MCP. What is it?
options: An open standard for connecting AI to tools and data
connectors.why: MCP is the Model Context Protocol.

connectors.q: Claude proposes creating an event in your calendar. Your job:
options: Read what it plans to do, then approve or change it
connectors.why: Claude asks before acting; you read before you approve.

options: A saved set of instructions Claude uses when a task matches or when you call it
skills.why: Teach Claude your way once, and it's always on hand.

skills.q: A good sign something should become a skill:
options: You've explained it to Claude twice
skills.why: Repeated explanations are the classic skill candidate.

skills.q: Your skill keeps missing one rule. Best fix:
options: Correct it, then ask Claude to update the skill
skills.why: Corrections in the skill stick; corrections in chat fade.

claudemd.q: When does Claude Code read a project's CLAUDE.md?
options: At the start of every session in that folder
claudemd.why: It's the standing rules Claude reads before every job.

options: Short: a map of where things live plus rules that prevent real mistakes
claudemd.why: Lean and goal-focused beats long and shouty.

claudemd.q: Where should an API key or password go?
options: In a secret store or environment variable, never in the repo
claudemd.why: Secrets stay out of files Claude and others read.

options: Claude Code itself: commands, panels, themes, checks

mods.q: Before installing a mod, you should:
options: Understand what it can see and change on your computer

mods.q: A mod hasn't helped in weeks. What now?
options: Remove it; a lean setup is part of the skill
mods.why: Keep only what earns its place.

duet.q: What does Claude Duet do before sending, paying, signing or deleting?
The most important part of setting up a background assistant:
options: Clear goals and ground rules for what it must never do without asking
duet.why: Goals plus ground rules make it safe and useful.

duet.q: A weekly summary has run fine for a month. Good practice:
options: Spot-check a few items against their sources now and then
duet.why: Trust grows from checks; keep checking.
